name: Minakari Enamel
author: Grok Bot
blurb: Ceremonial local-agent desk on an opaque cobalt enamel field: warm gold frames, a radial turquoise-and-vermilion flower, cream serif titles, and a plain sans for dense chat. Glazed and jewel-like. Not cloisonné wire, not chrome, not glass, not a pale blue card.

tagline.en: Cobalt glaze, a gold line, one flower
tagline.zh: 米纳卡里釉彩：钴蓝、金线、一朵花

origin.author: Grok Bot
origin.note: Authored by Grok Bot. Original Minakari Enamel system for a local-first agent named Glost. An interface interpretation of the craft's color and line, not a traditional artifact and not a copy of a workshop plate. Mood only, kept out of the repo: Design by Curio, Persian Minakari enamel (https://designbycurio.com/persian-minakari-enamel-isfahan and https://designbycurio.com/learn/persian-minakari-enamel-isfahan), for a saturated cobalt field, warm gold frames, turquoise and vermilion floral cells, and a radial flower. Craft, for what the material is: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Enamel (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/enamel/) describes heat-fused glass colored with metal oxides; from the mid-17th century, champlevé and enamel painting on gold, copper, and silver, later with royal blue, turquoise, and floral designs on gold or opaque grounds. Encyclopaedia Isfahanica, Enameling (https://en.isfahanica.org/entry/enameling-minakari-minasazi/) says painted enamel is the predominant Iranian technique and Isfahan is a principal center; khane-bandi (cloisonné) is a separate technique made in Isfahan in recent years, not the historical default; cobalt blue and turquoise are characteristic oxide colors; copper is the common base today, with gold and silver for finer pieces. Iranica, Isfahan xiii. Crafts (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/isfahan-xiii-crafts/) and Visit Iran (https://www.visitiran.ir/handicraft/enamel-brilliant-art-fire-earth-and-furnaces) place the living painted-enamel workshops in Isfahan. The gold line here is a painted frame, not a claim that minakari is cloisonné or gold-wire work. No third-party assets, screenshots, logos, markup, or copied text.
